newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec considering secondary stock exchange.
newsitem.headline: Quebec considering secondary stock exchange.

text.p: Quebec Finance Department officials are studying the possibility of setting up a secondary stock exchange to help small and medium-size companies raise capital, the Montreal newspaper La Presse reported on Monday.
Officials from Quebec Finance Minister Bernard Landry's office were not immediately available for comment.

Some Quebec mining, multimedia and biotechnology companies see their access to capital restricted by the rules of the Montreal Exchange, which is aimed more at well-established companies and does not necessarily attract investors looking for rising stars in the equities markets .
The idea of a secondary, smaller stock exchange has been around in Quebec for a while. It resurfaced most recently when Nasdaq examined the possibility of starting operations in Canada.

Such small stock exchanges already exist in London and Paris as well as at the Montreal Exchange's nearest competitor in Toronto, where the Toronto Stock Exchange operates the Canadian Dealing Network.
